solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expert in water, ocean, flexible at first

indicators.note: something flexible can be bent into a new shape, so the letters of ocean are rearranged

parts.note: first is written 1ST, and the figure 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at handling the sea, adaptable from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' reshapes OCEAN into CANOE; 'first' is written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler of a small boat is a practised hand on the water, so an expert in water describes one.

clue.text: Colourful singer is able to achieve recognition? Yes, initially

parts.note: is able to means can

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the three words achieve, recognition and Yes

explanation.surface: A flamboyant vocalist asks whether they can win acclaim, and answers yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a bright yellow songbird, a colourful singer kept in cages.

clue.text: Ahead of time, the writer's brought up Scottish island's story

indicators.note: puts the reversed island before the letter for time
in a down entry, brought up means read upwards, so the island's name runs backwards

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde
the writer's is the setter speaking of themself, I've (I have)

explanation.surface: Before long, the author has raised the tale of a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses the island, as this is a down entry. 'the writer's' is the setter speaking: I have, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a synonym of story.

clue.text: No longer a court, to be accurate

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer

explanation.surface: A former court must now be precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and accurate are synonyms, both meaning precisely correct.

clue.text: It's associated with IT skill — regularly one greatly admired

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word skill, starting with the first

parts.note: an icon is a person greatly admired and idolised

explanation.surface: Computer skill is regularly admired, the clue says.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'skill' gives S, I, L.
explanation.definitionFit: The element is the material of computer chips, hence Silicon Valley, home of information technology.

clue.text: Very few of scores usually expected in extremely strange setting

indicators.note: the outer letters act as a setting, as for a jewel, holding the golf term inside
extremely takes the extreme, outermost letters of the word strange

parts.note: in golf, par is the score usually expected on a hole; plural for scores

explanation.surface: Hardly any of the usual scores turned up in an odd setting.
explanation.walkthrough: PARS goes inside S...E, the ends of 'strange'. 'Very few' fits as an adjectival phrase: sparse visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered and scanty, so few in number.

clue.text: Map redone — rearranged walk

indicators.note: rearranged signals the letters of map redone are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A map has been redrawn, and the walking route rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a paved public walk, often along a seafront.

clue.text: Area for shooting practice in mountain chain

definitions.meaning: a place where people practise firing guns or arrows
a line of connected peaks, like the Andes

explanation.surface: A firing ground set among the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Range names both a shooting ground and a line of mountains, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Teen I try to reform for a long time!

indicators.note: to reform is to re-form, so the letters of teen I try are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A teenager's reform seems to take forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark shares the exasperation of a parent waiting for a teenager to reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, and colloquially any very long wait.

clue.text: As a rule, small number at motoring event Mike enters

indicators.note: places the number next to the event

parts.note: No. is the short form of number, hence small

indicators.note: the letter for Mike goes into the name of the motoring event

parts.note: a rally is a motoring competition on public roads
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Usually there are only a few cars at the rally when Mike turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally and as a rule both mean usually, under ordinary circumstances.

clue.text: Move quickly to accommodate old in waiting room

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the quick movement holds the abbreviation for old

parts.note: to lunge is to move forward suddenly

explanation.surface: Hurry to make space for the elderly in the waiting room.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport or station lounge is a room where travellers sit and wait.

clue.text: Fish deep

definitions.meaning: low in pitch, as a voice or note

explanation.definitionFit: Bass is a fish when it rhymes with mass and a low-pitched voice when it rhymes with base.

clue.text: Severely criticise meat maybe

definitions.meaning: a joint cooked in the oven, typically meat

explanation.surface: Slate the meat, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast is slang for harsh criticism and also names a joint of oven-cooked meat.

clue.text: Fickle person taking tea with me before Christmas comes round

indicators.note: the tea takes on, gains the word me after it
puts that pair in front of the turned-round festival

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

indicators.note: comes round means the word for Christmas is turned backwards

parts.note: Noel is another name for Christmas

explanation.surface: An inconstant friend drops in for tea with me before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' turns the festival's name backwards; 'before' looks like timing but places the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard changes colour to match its surroundings, so the name is used for a person who keeps changing opinions.

clue.text: Fruit of obtrusively religious, very quiet, home?

parts.note: pi is British slang for sanctimonious or ostentatiously devout
pp is pianissimo, the music marking for very quiet
in means at home

explanation.surface: Is the produce of the pious, hushed household any good?
explanation.walkthrough: PI (short for pious) is British slang for showily devout.
explanation.definitionFit: A pippin is a variety of eating apple, such as Cox's Orange Pippin.

clue.text: One annoyingly smug about unpleasant people ultimately right?

indicators.note: the prig goes about, around the word for unpleasant

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous, smug person
vile means very unpleasant

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of people

explanation.surface: A smug person goes on about nasty people, and asks if that's fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the smug person around the nastiness; 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'people'.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or advantage granted to some.

clue.text: Colour of vehicle learner included in matching collection

indicators.note: the vehicle and learner go inside the matching collection

parts.note: a set is a group of matching items
a car is a motor vehicle
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: The shade of a learner's car in a matching collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red, a colour.

clue.text: New cute rival paying well

indicators.note: new means the letters of cute rival are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A charming new competitor is making good money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative work is profitable, bringing in plenty of money.

clue.text: Joking about island feature encountered on way up?

indicators.note: the joking goes about, around the abbreviation for island

parts.note: banter is playful joking talk

explanation.surface: Jokes about an island landmark that you meet on the climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way up' sounds like a mountain path, but it is a staircase; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The handrail of a staircase is something you meet as you climb the stairs.

clue.text: Useful service — the last word, pity to miss introduction!

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the last word

indicators.note: missing its introduction means the opening letter of the word pity is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing its opening letter

explanation.surface: A handy facility, the final word: what a shame to skip the opening!
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a useful or pleasant facility, such as a pool or a shop.

clue.text: Ready for change when daughter's gone for period

indicators.note: for change means the letters of ready are rearranged

explanation.surface: All set to change once the daughter has left for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle READY with the D of daughter gone, as 'gone' says: the remaining E, R, A, Y rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time, twelve months.

clue.text: British sweep seen as an infringement

parts.note: reach and sweep both mean extent or range

explanation.surface: A British sweeping move is seen as an infringement.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a violation of a law or agreement, an infringement.

clue.text: Direct route not the original policy, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: not the original, a fallback, is plan B, so the policy is a B line

explanation.surface: The straight way is not the first policy, we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: The second option is the B, as in plan B, and a policy is a line, so 'B line' is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is the straightest path, as a bee is supposed to fly home.

clue.text: Notice article, become very angry

parts.note: to notice is to see
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Spot the item and fly into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to boil with rage, being very angry.

clue.text: Bring about a sit-in — get organised

indicators.note: organised signals the letters of a sit-in and get are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Start a protest occupation and get it properly arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to set something in motion, to cause it.

clue.text: Slight change in team in end, one Pole swapped for another

indicators.note: change in says the team's name is altered

indicators.text: in end, one Pole swapped for another
indicators.note: the final letter, S for the south pole, is replaced by N for the north

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: A minor change in the side at the end, one Polish player replacing another.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the London football club Tottenham Hotspur. 'Pole' looks like a Polish player, but means a compass pole: S becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub them, as to spurn is to reject with contempt.

clue.text: Singular, healthy, variety of gas

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A single, healthy kind of gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale gas is natural gas extracted from layered rock, so the rock names a kind of gas.

clue.text: Famous person clasping India's instrument — this one?

indicators.note: the famous person clasps, holds, the letter for India

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A celebrity holds India's instrument and wonders if it's this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this one?' asks whether the instrument meant is India's own, which the stringed lute is.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked lute of Indian classical music.

clue.text: Kick about leading English? It's an artificial high point!

indicators.note: the kick goes about the word for leading

parts.note: to toe a ball is to kick it with the toe
up means ahead, leading, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A kick-about with the English in front, and something fake on top!
explanation.walkthrough: 'high point' sounds like a peak, but it is the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpiece worn on the crown is a false covering for the top of the head.

clue.text: Locality I'd recalled, harsh

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters of I'd run backwards

parts.note: strict means harsh, severe

explanation.surface: I remembered the area as a harsh one.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area or neighbourhood, a locality.

clue.text: Soldier more candid after last of staff leaves

indicators.note: leaves means the letter goes away from the comparative

parts.note: franker means more candid, more open

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of staff

explanation.surface: A soldier speaks more openly once the last of the staff has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranker is a soldier in the ranks, an ordinary private rather than an officer.

clue.text: Referring to voting system that is vulnerable at edges results in postponement

parts.note: re means concerning, referring to
PR is proportional representation
i.e. is id est, that is

indicators.note: at edges takes the outermost letters of the word vulnerable

explanation.surface: Talk of an electoral system that's shaky at its margins leads to a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a stay of punishment, a postponement or cancellation.
